LESSON: READING 4.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: VISUALS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to interpret visuals correctly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read visuals in print and digital formats for information

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 4.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: VISUALS
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 4.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: VISUALS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read visuals in print and digital formats for information

What this means
In this part you learn to read visuals in print and digital formats for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read visuals in print and digital formats for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read visuals in print and digital formats for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read visuals in print and digital formats for information)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read visuals in print and digital formats for information.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to interpret visuals correctly?
2. How do visuals like photos and videos enhance our understanding of a text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read visuals in print and digital formats for information.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
